chunks: Sa'd narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Ali al-Halabi; and al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abi al-Sabbah al-Kinani; and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-Muthanna al-Hannat, from Abi Basir; all together from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, concerning:

A man who recites in the obligatory salat (prayer) half of a surah, then forgets and begins another until he finishes it, then remembers before he performs ruku' (bowing) — he said: “He should perform ruku', and it does not harm him.”

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, said: “And whoever forgets a sajdah (prostration),” up to his statement, “and whoever speaks” — its explanation has already passed in the chapter before this chapter, so there is no point in repeating it.

Then he said, may Allah have mercy on him: Whoever speaks deliberately in the salat (prayer) with that speech which is not permitted in the salat (prayer), he must repeat it; and whoever speaks forgetfully must perform the two sajdahs of forgetfulness, and the repetition of the salat (prayer) is not required of him.

key_terms.إِعَادَةُ الصَّلَاةِ: repeating the salat due to invalidation
key_terms.السُّورَةِ: a chapter of the Qur'an being recited in salat
key_terms.سَجْدَتَيِ السَّهْوِ: the two prostrations performed to compensate for forgetfulness in salat
key_terms.يَرْكَعُ: he performs ruku' (bowing) in the prayer

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone forgets during recitation or speaks unintentionally in salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses rulings of forgetfulness in salat (prayer). It states that if a person mistakenly moves from half of one surah to another and remembers before ruku' (bowing), the salat remains valid, and it also distinguishes between deliberate speech, which invalidates the salat, and forgetful speech, which requires only the two sajdahs of forgetfulness.
